clue.text: Senior politician's in torment, if seat is in jeopardy

indicators.note: something in jeopardy is under threat of being upset, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe-s read as the verb is
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A government grandee is in agony because his parliamentary seat might be lost at the election.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 's (read as IS) plus torment, if and seat; the 'in' before torment is only glue for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A Minister of State is a middle-ranking UK government post, a senior politician just below cabinet rank.

clue.text: Local ranch where Incas ate, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters only possibly stand as written, so another arrangement of them is wanted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A South American cattle ranch where the Incas once took their meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' points to the Spanish-speaking Americas, the same part of the world as the Incas, where the word is in everyday use.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large cattle estate in Argentina and neighbouring Spanish-speaking countries, the regional term for a ranch.

clue.text: Demand by miners after a strike

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an assertion of a right, as in a pay demand
second meaning: the plot prospectors stake once they strike gold

explanation.surface: Union miners put in a demand once their industrial action is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The strike looks like a walkout by a coal union; it is a prospector's strike of gold, after which the plot is staked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a demand for something owed and the piece of land a prospector marks out as his own.

clue.text: Any crest may indicate it

indicators.note: may signals only a possibility, inviting the solver to try another arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family crest on a shield can reveal where someone comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a heraldic crest records a family's line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic crests were granted to families and passed down, so one shows a person's lineage.

clue.text: Chap seen in an uprising in deserted state

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising makes the letters climb, so they read from bottom to top
seen in places the chap within the following short word

parts.note: taken as written
a typical man's name for a chap

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a revolt in an abandoned country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is a US state covered largely by desert, so a deserted state in the sense of a desert one.

clue.text: No intention of going to court

definitions.text: No intention of going to court

parts.words: No intention of going to court
parts.note: surface reading: someone with no plan to sue
setter's reading: courting a lover, which someone unattached and carefree has no thought of

explanation.walkthrough: Court looks legal, but it is courtship: the phrase describes a person with no romantic attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free from the ties of love has no wish to woo anybody, hence no plans to court.

clue.text: Lady bareback rider

parts.note: surface reading: a woman riding a horse without a saddle
setter's reading: a lady whose back, and everything else, was bare as she rode through Coventry

explanation.walkthrough: Legend says this Lady rode naked through Coventry; 'bareback' describes the rider, not the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh-century noblewoman of legend rode through the streets unclothed, protesting her husband's taxes.

clue.text: Attractive range shown in traveller's guide

parts.note: attracting like a magnet
compass as scope or extent

explanation.surface: An appealing mountain range featured in a guidebook for tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'traveller's guide' is not a book but an instrument; both halves of the wordplay keep their literal sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle-based instrument pointing north helps people find their way, guiding travellers across unknown ground.

clue.text: Cheek to have one in pub before church

indicators.note: in puts the word for one inside the word for a pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole means the only one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: It's a bit rich to drink in the pub before going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: One is not I here but SOLE, as in the sole survivor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is rude, disrespectful boldness, which is exactly what insolence means.

clue.text: Wool drops a point in the market

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so a letter is lost from the wool

parts.note: angora is wool from rabbits or goats
N is north, a compass point

explanation.surface: The price of wool falls a point at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops a point' reads like trading news; the point is a compass point taken out of the wool.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square of an ancient Greek city, where trading and assemblies took place.

clue.text: Fancy silver in one place of gold, perhaps

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in sets the metal inside the place where gold is dug

parts.note: a gold mine; perhaps because other things are mined too
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An ornate silver piece set in a golden setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the silverware; it is the verb meaning to picture something.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to suppose or picture it in your mind, which is to form an image of it.

clue.text: Where lots go despite rising prices

definitions.text: Where lots go despite rising prices

parts.words: Where lots go despite rising prices
parts.note: surface reading: plenty of people still go somewhere though it is getting expensive
setter's reading: lots are items for sale, which go to the highest bidder as bids climb

explanation.walkthrough: Lots means many people in the surface; really it is the numbered items in a sale, which are sold because the bidding rises.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale in which goods are sold to whoever bids most is where numbered lots change hands.

clue.text: Robin Hood's favourite sweets?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the jolly friar among Robin Hood's band of outlaws
second meaning: British school slang for sweets and snacks

explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jovial monk among Robin Hood's merry men; in British school slang tuck means sweets and snacks, sold at a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the outlaw's friar companion is also a British word for confectionery eaten by pupils.

clue.text: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low

definitions.text: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low

parts.words: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low
parts.note: surface reading: a complaint about falling quality
setter's reading: standards are flags, flown lowered as a sign of mourning

explanation.walkthrough: Standards are flags, not levels of quality; flags are lowered partway down the pole after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags flown partway down the pole mark national mourning, a time when no one celebrates.

clue.text: His contribution to knowledge is past understanding

definitions.text: His contribution to knowledge is past understanding

parts.words: His contribution to knowledge is past understanding
parts.note: surface reading: a scholar whose work is incomprehensible
setter's reading: an understanding of the past is what this scholar supplies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Past understanding' means beyond comprehension on the surface; read literally, it is knowledge of bygone times.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies and writes about earlier times adds to what we know about the past.

clue.text: Truth awkward, try a lie

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and ill-placed, so the following letters need setting in a better order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: When the truth is uncomfortable, someone suggests telling a lie instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Reality is the state of things as they actually are, which is the truth.

clue.text: Cast pie out, though it's germ-free

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a pie even though it is perfectly clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic describes conditions kept free of harmful bacteria, as in surgery, so free of germs.

clue.text: Heroic Greek units holding an elevated position

indicators.note: holding means the units grip the raised position inside them

parts.note: an ace is a one, a single unit, on cards and dice
a hill is high ground

explanation.surface: Brave Greek troops keep control of a strategic height.
explanation.walkthrough: Units looks military, matching the heroic Greek, but it means ones, which are aces.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the greatest warrior of the Greeks at Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Speculations arise when he is accepted by the Conservative Party

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the party wraps around the short word

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rumours start when a man is admitted into the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are ideas put forward to explain something but not yet proven, which is what speculations are.

clue.text: Early morning 9 across today

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dawn, when daylight first appears
second meaning: 9 across is the opening entry of this puzzle, and an entry in a crossword grid is called a light

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference does not ask for the answer to 9 across; it points at where that clue sits, the first light in today's grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is when daylight first appears, and the opening grid entry of the day's puzzle is literally its first crossword light.

clue.text: Payment received by letter

parts.note: surface reading: money that arrives through the post
setter's reading: a letter is someone who lets out property, a landlord

explanation.walkthrough: Letter looks like post; it is one who lets, and what a landlord collects is the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum paid by a tenant for use of a property is the income a landlord takes in.

clue.text: Man is, whatever Donne says

parts.note: surface reading: a rebuttal of John Donne's line that no man stands alone
setter's reading: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.walkthrough: The poet John Donne wrote 'No man is an island'; the Isle of Man, a British crown dependency, certainly is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is a piece of land surrounded by sea, contradicting the famous line of Donne's sermon.

clue.text: Planned mode of protest

indicators.note: something planned is worked out and organised, so these letters are set in a deliberate new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A carefully organised form of protest action.
explanation.definitionFit: Demo is the short form of demonstration, a public march or rally against something.

clue.text: Place for landing and take-off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a landing ... for aircraft
second meaning: to take off clothes, read as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Landing and take-off sound like one aviation phrase; take-off is a separate meaning, to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a runway where planes touch down, and to undress is to remove your clothes.

clue.text: A growing attachment to climbers

parts.note: surface reading: an increasing fondness for mountaineers
setter's reading: climbing plants, which cling to supports with a slender growing shoot

explanation.walkthrough: Climbers are plants, not mountaineers, and the attachment is a physical one that grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender coiling shoot that a climbing plant uses to grip supports is literally a growing attachment.

clue.text: Goes flat out arranging tenancies to rent

parts.note: a landlord lets property, arranging a tenancy
rent as the past of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A landlord rushes about setting up leases to let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is not payment here but a tear, as in rending cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting without restraint, such as driving at full speed.

clue.text: A capital investment

parts.note: surface reading: putting money into a business
setter's reading: capital means of the head, and to invest is to clothe or adorn

explanation.walkthrough: Capital comes from the Latin for head, and invest can mean to robe someone, so this is an ornament put on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown-like ornament worn by a woman on her head is headgear she is adorned with.

clue.text: Denis seen to be wanting

indicators.note: to be hints that the letters are yet to become something else, a gentle signal to rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Denis appears to be lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' reads as an adjective in the surface; as the definition it is the noun, the condition of lacking things.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting as a noun is a state of want or poverty, the condition of being in need.
